findings.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:78 — The setup endpoint response now includes a `backupCodes` field with plaintext one-time backup codes, an unversioned response-shape change that existing callers won't consume and that permanently exposes sensitive codes to any client/logging layer not expecting this field

apps/web/components/settings/TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts:22 — disable()` signature changed from `(password, code)` to `(password, code, backupCode)`, a breaking change for any other caller of this shared client function that isn't updated to pass the new required-positional argument

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:65 — The credentials provider gained a new `backupCode` field; since NextAuth credential field lists can be introspected/rendered by generic sign-in UIs and third-party NextAuth clients, this is a public contract change to the auth provider metadata with no versioning or migration note

apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:48 — disable.ts` now silently branches on `req.body.backupCode` truthiness without validating type/format before use at line 58, so malformed non-string payloads (contract violation) fail with an unhandled runtime error rather than a documented 400 error code

apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58 — JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` is unguarded, so corrupted/legacy ciphertext or a decrypt/JSON error throws an unhandled exception instead of returning a graceful error response.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:78 — The setup endpoint response now includes a `backupCodes` field with plaintext one-time backup codes, an unversioned response-shape change that existing callers won't consume and that permanently exposes sensitive codes to any client/logging layer not expecting this field

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably change `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` to return plaintext `backupCodes` in the JSON response (`return res.json({ secret, keyUri, dataUri, backupCodes });`). That is a sensitive-field exposure and an API response-shape change. However, the PR also updates the primary in-repo caller (`EnableTwoFactorModal`) to consume/display/download those codes, so it’s not clearly a correctness break within this diff, and claims about “existing callers” or “permanent exposure to logging layers” aren’t directly evidenced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/components/settings/TwoFactorAuthAPI.ts:22 — disable()` signature changed from `(password, code)` to `(password, code, backupCode)`, a breaking change for any other caller of this shared client function that isn't updated to pass the new required-positional argument

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable` changed to require a third positional argument (`backupCode`) and the one updated call site in `DisableTwoFactorModal` now passes it. However, the finding claims this is a breaking change for “any other caller” that wasn’t updated, but the diff does not show any other callers (or whether this function is used elsewhere). From the diff alone, we can’t verify that anything is broken or un-updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:65 — The credentials provider gained a new `backupCode` field; since NextAuth credential field lists can be introspected/rendered by generic sign-in UIs and third-party NextAuth clients, this is a public contract change to the auth provider metadata with no versioning or migration note

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a new `backupCode` entry to the NextAuth Credentials provider `credentials` metadata (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts), which will change the provider metadata returned by NextAuth and potentially affect any generic sign-in UIs/clients that render fields from that list. This is a compatibility/contract surface change rather than an immediate runtime defect, and the diff itself contains no accompanying note or mitigation for external consumers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:48 — disable.ts` now silently branches on `req.body.backupCode` truthiness without validating type/format before use at line 58, so malformed non-string payloads (contract violation) fail with an unhandled runtime error rather than a documented 400 error code

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` treats any truthy `backupCode` as usable and then calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")`. If a client sends a malformed non-string JSON value (e.g., object/number/array) that is truthy, `replaceAll` will be undefined and cause an unhandled runtime exception (500) rather than returning a controlled `400` error code. The diff shows no type/format validation or guarding before `replaceAll`/`indexOf` use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58 — JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` is unguarded, so corrupted/legacy ciphertext or a decrypt/JSON error throws an unhandled exception instead of returning a graceful error response.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode`, the code does `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY));` with no try/catch. Even though it checks `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `user.backupCodes` existence, `symmetricDecrypt(...)` (bad/legacy/corrupted ciphertext) or `JSON.parse(...)` (non-JSON plaintext) can still throw, which will propagate out of the handler as an unhandled exception and yield a generic 500 rather than a controlled JSON error response.
